closure_target: complete contractor and subcontractor certification, records-request, investigation, suspension, debarment, litigation, settlement, and no-action roster
coverage_statement: Executive Order 14398, FAR implementation, OFCCP programme disposition, the Civil Rights Fraud Initiative, and the IBM resolution expose contractor clauses, certification, records, investigation, suspension, debarment, False Claims Act, settlement, and remediation mechanisms. They do not expose the complete contractor and subcontractor universe or all action and no-action rows.
included_rows: Civil Rights Fraud Initiative enforcement architecture
one named contractor investigation and settlement with remediation
unavailable_rows: all certifications, records requests, referrals, investigations, sanctions, settlements, appeals, declinations, and no-action rows
complete contract, agency, amount, timing, and recurrence denominator
refused_rows: one settlement is not treated as enforcement prevalence
clause applicability is not treated as observed certification or violation
contractor status is not treated as liability, coordination, or common purpose
negative_search_statement: The source set exposes the operative contractor architecture and one named resolution but not the complete covered-entity and action denominator.
correction_route: FAR Council and agency deviation records
SAM.gov, contracting-office, suspension and debarment, and False Claims Act records
Boards of Contract Appeals, GAO, Court of Federal Claims, and judicial review

closure_target: complete disparate-impact and related civil-rights enforcement, declination, guidance, referral, withdrawal, and replacement-rule ledger
coverage_statement: Executive Order 14281, DOJ guidance and final rule, dismissals, compliance reviews, investigations, agreements, and joint technical assistance expose bounded changes to disparate-impact and related civil-rights enforcement. They do not provide the complete enforcement, declination, referral, withdrawal, replacement-rule, affected-sector, comparator, and no-action ledger.
included_rows: disparate-impact deprioritization and Title VI rule change
employment technical assistance and litigation dismissals
named grant and scholarship compliance reviews
named environmental settlement and litigation dispositions
unavailable_rows: all referrals, guidance, withdrawals, replacement rules, investigations, settlements, appeals, and no-action rows
complete timing, staffing, budget, and recurrence records
refused_rows: press releases are not substituted for complete case files or enforcement ledgers
named actions are not treated as prevalence or uniform implementation
investigation announcements are not treated as findings of violation
negative_search_statement: The official sources establish a bounded set of rule, guidance, investigation, dismissal, settlement, and programme-disposition rows but not the complete civil-rights enforcement denominator.
correction_route: DOJ, EEOC, agency civil-rights, and Federal Register records
case dockets, settlement instruments, and compliance-review files
administrative, judicial, inspector-general, congressional, and rulemaking review

closure_target: regulated-entity appeal, protest, litigation, settlement, remedy, timing, access, cost, recurrence, and durability ledger
coverage_statement: Ames, VMD, IBM, PayPal, Minnesota, Illinois, UVA, and Cornell expose bounded judicial, procurement, settlement, programme, and compliance-review correction outcomes. They do not provide a complete regulated-entity appeal, protest, litigation, remedy, timing, access, cost, recurrence, and durability ledger.
included_rows: False Claims Act and fair-lending settlements
university agreements and investigation pauses or closures
unavailable_rows: complete appeal, protest, litigation, settlement, and remedy universe
practical access, cost, timing, compliance, recurrence, reversal, and durability rows
complete denied, abandoned, unresolved, and no-remedy rows
refused_rows: formal correction is not treated as effective or durable correction without outcome evidence
settlement is not treated as admission of liability unless the instrument says so
bounded controls are not treated as system-wide remedy adequacy
negative_search_statement: The source set exposes multiple correction mechanisms and outcomes but not the complete practical-correction denominator.
correction_route: independent audit, judicial enforcement, procurement review, and public reporting
